newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court advises case-by-case review on 'economic activity'.
newsitem.headline: Court advises case-by-case review on 'economic activity'.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said national courts must evaluate all the circumstances surrounding an individual case when determining if the hiring out of vehicles is economic activity under the Sixth VAT directive.

A German taxpayer purchased a motor caravan ostensibly for the purpose of hiring it out to earn an income. After two years, she had hired the car out primarily to her husband's business. She rented the caravan out to third parties a total of four times in two years, according to court documents.
The court reviewed the method for characterizing "economic activity" under the Sixth VAT directive and said such activity does not include those carried out on an occasional basis.
In order for the hiring out of property to be considered "exploitation of property" under the directive, and hence an economic activity, it must be done on a continuing basis.

The burden of establishing eligibility for VAT deduction rests with the taxpayer, the court said. Judicial authorities should review evidence to see whether or not the purpose of the activity is to obtain income, not whether the tax payer acutally was successful.
The court said the nature of the property may be considered, as well as how it is used, when analyzing if the taxpayer sought to obtain income from it.

"If by reason of its nature, property is capable of being used for both economic and private purposes, all the circumstances in which it is used will have to be examined in order to determine whether it is actually used for the pupose of obtaining income on a regular basis," the court said.

The court suggested comparing the actual use of the property to a standard use to ascertain if the activity was in fact one carried out for obtaining income on a continuing basis. Additionally, the actual length of time the property is hired, the number of customers and the earnings received should be considered.
EXCERPTS FROM THE COURT
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: German)
"Sixth VAT directive - Definition of economic activity - Taxable amount"
In Case C-230/94
26 September 1996
Reference by the Bundesfinanzhof for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending before that court between
Renate Enkler
and
Finanzamt Homburg

on the interpretation of article 4(1) and (2), 6(2)(a) and 11A(1)(c) of the Sixth Council directive (77/388/EEC) of 17 May 1977 onthe harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment (OJ 1977 L 145, p. 1)
THE COURT hereby rules

1. The hiring of tangible property constitutes exploitation of such property which must be classified as an "economic activity" within the meaing of article 4(2) of the Sixth Council directive (77/388/EEC) of 17 May 1977 onthe harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment, if it is done for the purpose of obtaining income therefrom ona continuing basis.

2. In order to determine whether the hiring out of tangible property such as a motor caravan is carried on with a view to obtaining income on a continuing basis, within the meaning of the second sentence of article 4(2) of the Sixth directive, it is for the national court to evaluate all the circumstances of the particular case.

3. Article 11A(1)(c) of the Sixth Council directive is to be interpreted as meaning that the taxable amount for turnover tax on transactions treated as supplies of services under Article 6(2)(a) of the directive must include expenses which are incurred during a period in which the goods are at the taxable person's disposal in a way that he can actually use them at any time for non-business purposes and which related to the goods themselves or which the taxable person is entitled to deduct for VAT purposes. The portion of the expenses to be included must be proportionate to the ration between the total duration of actual use of the goods and the duration of actual use for non-business purposes.
